title: Evaluate Micro-Pilot — 10 R-Series Classification & Feasibility Analysis
status: RESEARCH COMPLETE — All 10 items classified. Evaluate upgrade feasible for all but requires stem+distractor+EC rewrite per S836 pipeline.

preconditions.target: 10 Evaluate items from S839 Cohort C (Pack E R-series)

methodology: Per-item read from pack_e_corrected.js — Stem, CorrectChoice, Choices, ExplanationCorrect, ExplanationWrongA-D, CognitiveLevel, DifficultyScore. Classified as READY/NEEDS ENHANCEMENT/NOT SUITABLE based on whether existing scenario supports judgment-level decision without substantial stem rewrite.

results.assessment: All 10 R-series items have well-constructed business scenarios (named companies, specific stakeholders, realistic control contexts). However, every item currently tests at Bloom's Apply classification/identification level. The stems ask candidates to identify, classify, or describe — not to evaluate, recommend, or choose among competing valid options with trade-offs. The Evaluate upgrade is FEASIBLE for all 10 but requires substantial rewrite.

per_item_classification.scenario_quality: HIGH — specific employee tasks, rich context
per_item_classification.upgrade_path: From 'what is the weakness?' to 'which restructuring recommendation best addresses the risk given staffing constraints?'

per_item_classification.scenario_quality: HIGH — multiple red flags (financial strain, override access, no vacation policy)
per_item_classification.upgrade_path: From 'which element?' to 'which mitigation action should audit committee prioritize?'
Add staffing constraint (3 clerks); pivot to 'which workflow restructure best balances SoD and efficiency?'

per_item_classification.topic: Tone at the top / control environment
per_item_classification.scenario_quality: HIGH — CEO quotes, promotion patterns, board concern
per_item_classification.upgrade_path: From 'which component is weakened?' to 'which board response most effectively addresses the control environment weakness while preserving business momentum?'

per_item_classification.scenario_quality: HIGHEST — natural trade-off context (4 staff, limited budget, owner reviews)
per_item_classification.upgrade_path: Owner considering 3 additional measures with budget constraint — which provides greatest incremental risk reduction?

per_item_classification.scenario_quality: MEDIUM — three named controls, purely classification
per_item_classification.upgrade_path: Keep controls as context; ask 'which additional detective control best complements existing preventive framework?'
Add volume constraint (500 claims/day); pivot to 'which additional detective control is most efficient?'

per_item_classification.scenario_quality: HIGH — four concrete board-level options already enumerated
per_item_classification.upgrade_path: Add constraints (rural hospital, $200K IT budget); pivot to 'which risk response strategy should the board prioritize?'
Add 3-clerk constraint; pivot to 'which assignment structure best balances SoD and operational efficiency?'

per_item_classification.scenario_quality: HIGH — specific $ values, hedging program, dual-approval requirements
per_item_classification.upgrade_path: Add risk appetite ($300K); pivot to 'residual exceeds appetite — which recommendation addresses the gap?'

evaluate_upgrade_requirements.stem_rewrite: From classification to recommendation: replace 'Which of the following best describes...' with 'Which recommendation should [stakeholder] present to [board/management] given [constraints]?'
evaluate_upgrade_requirements.distractor_rewrite: From single-error identification to competing-recommendation distractors. Each must be plausibly defensible but suboptimal under COSO principles and operational constraints.
evaluate_upgrade_requirements.ec_rewrite: From concept identification to judgment rationale — including trade-off analysis, constraint assessment, criterion-based decision justification, and COSO framework alignment.
evaluate_upgrade_requirements.correct_choice: All current answer keys are correct. No CorrectChoice changes needed — the upgrade changes question FORMAT, not underlying accounting truth.
evaluate_upgrade_requirements.difficulty: DS=3 (Moderate) may need upgrade to DS=4 (Difficult) for Evaluate-level items

wave_plan.wave_1_rationale: Strongest business decision context — each has natural trade-offs and constraints that support genuine judgment.
wave_plan.wave_3_rationale: Classification-focused items — may be better suited for Analyze upgrade rather than Evaluate.

comparison_to_s845_cohort_a.s845_analyze_upgrade: 22 items — enhances existing content with analysis layer
comparison_to_s845_cohort_a.s846_evaluate_upgrade: 10 items — requires stem format change (classification → recommendation)
comparison_to_s845_cohort_a.relative_difficulty: S846 is 2-3x more effort per item than S845 because the question FORMAT changes, not just the explanation layer
